# Template text built from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/template-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-1336](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data that becomes the source text of a template (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta
REST):

- FreeMarker: the source of a `Template` (a `String` or `Reader`) and a `StringTemplateLoader`
  entry;
- Velocity: the template text given to `evaluate`;
- Thymeleaf: the template given to `TemplateEngine.process` (text with the default string
  resolver, a template name with a file or class-path resolver).

Request data passed in the data model or context is fine and not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Template languages run code on the server. A FreeMarker template can create objects with `?new`,
Velocity templates can call methods on the objects they reach, and Thymeleaf evaluates SpEL or OGNL
expressions. A client who writes the template text can therefore run code on the server or read
its data.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the greeting text from the request is compiled as a FreeMarker template.

```java
package com.example.mail;

import freemarker.template.Configuration;
import freemarker.template.Template;
import freemarker.template.TemplateException;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.StringReader;
import java.util.Map;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServlet;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;

public class GreetingServlet extends HttpServlet {
    private final Configuration cfg = new Configuration(Configuration.VERSION_2_3_32);

    @Override
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response) throws IOException {
        Template template = new Template("greeting", new StringReader(request.getParameter("text")), cfg);
        try {
            template.process(Map.of("user", request.getRemoteUser()), response.getWriter());
        } catch (TemplateException e) {
            response.sendError(400);
        }
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the template is a file of the application; the text is a value in the data model.

```java
package com.example.mail;

import freemarker.template.Configuration;
import freemarker.template.Template;
import freemarker.template.TemplateException;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.Map;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServlet;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;

public class GreetingServlet extends HttpServlet {
    private final Configuration cfg = new Configuration(Configuration.VERSION_2_3_32);

    @Override
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response) throws IOException {
        Template template = cfg.getTemplate("greeting.ftlh");
        try {
            template.process(Map.of("text", request.getParameter("text")), response.getWriter());
        } catch (TemplateException e) {
            response.sendError(400);
        }
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep templates in the application: a constant, or a file loaded by name (`cfg.getTemplate(...)`,
  a Thymeleaf view name).
- Pass request data in the data model or context (`model.put(...)`, `context.put(...)`,
  `ctx.setVariable(...)`), where it is only data.
- If users choose between templates, pick one from an allow-list.
- Sandbox settings (a FreeMarker `TemplateClassResolver`, Velocity's `SecureUberspector`) are not
  enough to make user-written templates safe.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)
- Apache FreeMarker
- Apache Velocity
- Thymeleaf

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Thymeleaf's template resolver is not seen, so a request value given to `process` is reported
  whether the engine reads it as template text or as a template name.
- Spring MVC view names are not checked: recent Thymeleaf versions refuse to run view names taken
  from the URL, and the view technology is not visible here.
- For FreeMarker's `Template(name, sourceName, reader, cfg)`, a request value as the source name
  (only a label in error messages) is quiet when the reader is visibly a `Reader`; with a reader
  returned by a call, the source name is reported.
- Sandbox settings do not stop the finding: the FreeMarker FAQ lists other risks as well.
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source, and one method is analysed at a time.
  Allow-list lookups are recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants and as `valueOf` of an enum
  declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/java/template/template-injection.java`](../../../rules/java/template/template-injection.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/java/template/template-injection.yml`](../../../rules/java/template/template-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
